_note: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the whole site — the only data file in the app. Shaped as DB TABLES, not as a tree: `layouts` and `hotspots` are sibling arrays and a hotspot names its parent with `layoutId` (the foreign key). The nesting the Resources panel shows is rebuilt at load by src/config/index.ts, and the engine's scene/destination structure is projected at import by src/shared/scene-data/adapter.ts — nothing is generated to disk, so no value exists here twice. Each top-level key maps to one table or one settings row: meta/assets/world/cameras/lights/globals are the site record, zones/tones/copy are its presentation, layouts and hotspots are the two content tables.

assets._note: TWO MODELS, ONE ZONE. `modelUrl` is the DOLLHOUSE model — a decimated whole-zone GLB drawn in one go, which is the right answer for a fixed vantage that frames everything at once. The walking view does not use it: it streams the chunk set in `stream` instead. `previewUrl` is the point-cloud silhouette shown behind the loading HUD and must be baked FROM `modelUrl` — it is that model dissolving in, so a preview of any other mesh draws a cloud at the wrong scale and in the wrong place. 60,000 points, bounds x -2156..-64 / z -875..969, which is the 25-compressed GLB's own extent. There is no `navmeshUrl` here: the bake emits the navmesh alongside the chunks, so it travels with them (and follows NEXT_PUBLIC_ASSET_BASE to a CDN) rather than being a second copy someone has to keep in step. Set it only for a site with no `stream` block.

_note: ADAPTIVE CHUNK STREAMING — THE WALKING VIEW ONLY. The model is cut into
816 object chunks, each baked at three quality tiers, and the distance
from the camera decides which tier a chunk is loaded at — or whether it
is loaded at all.
near = good · mid = medium · far = low · beyond far = not loaded
The DOLLHOUSE does not stream: it draws `assets.modelUrl`, one decimated
whole-zone GLB. Streaming is a bad trade from a fixed vantage that frames
the entire zone — the view cone covers everything, so the frustum cull
buys nothing and the bands only fight the byte ceiling, whose eviction
drops the FURTHEST chunk first, i.e. exactly the half of the frame the
shot is composed around. The streamer mounts on the way in to first
person, under the entry blackout, and fills in around `cameras.spawn`
before the fade lifts.
The asset set is baked in the LA_PORT_ADAPTIVE repo (`npm run bake
portla-c5-v5-obj`) and staged under public/assets/<slug>/assets/, which
is gitignored — set NEXT_PUBLIC_ASSET_BASE to serve it from a CDN.
NO PALETTE, BUT THE CRANES MOVE. v5-obj is the object-chunked bake of
la-port-zone-c5-model-v5.glb with `chunking.instancing` OFF and
`animation` ON. So there is no palette.glb and no instances.bin — every
byte of geometry is a chunk under the LRU, nothing pinned — but there IS
an animated.glb: 2 clips (CraneCycle, CraneCycle.001), 1,752 mesh nodes,
192,150 triangles, 1.4 MB, lifted out of the chunks and permanently
resident. It has to be: a chunk bakes the node matrix into its vertices,
and an animation is exactly a moving node matrix. StreamedModel steps its
mixer EVERY frame rather than on the 10 Hz streaming tick, or the cranes
visibly stutter. The instancing path stays inert (initInstancing bails on
the manifest before it makes a request), which is what it was written for.
NAVMESH-V2 ships with this bake and is NOT the v1 that came with v4-obj:
3,988 -> 3,950 triangles, and it fragments into 55 islands where v1 was
one. `cameras.spawn` moved 26.8 m because v4's point landed in one of the
new holes — see the note on that block. The island count is the thing to
watch: a route between two points that used to connect may not any more.
Only `tiers.*.distance`, `tiers.*.texture`, `streaming.*`, `cache.*` and
`fog` are read live by the browser — edit and reload. The geometry LODs,
the texture rungs and the chunking itself are baked into files and need a
re-bake over in that repo.
MEASURED on this asset set: 12,848,173 source triangles / 26,124 mesh
nodes -> 816 chunks, all 816 carrying geometry, + the animated rig. 86 MB
of chunk GLBs + 26.5 MB of texture rungs, 69 images, 186 materials. It
reconciles exactly: 12,656,023 chunk near-tris + 192,150 lifted into
animated.glb = 12,848,173 = source, zero instanced. Worst case at these
bands (360°, no frustum cull): peak 11.33 M tris, 26.5 MB encoded,
358 MB decoded, 32.2 MB of WebP texture VRAM — ~391 MB total. With the
frustum cull on, the real resident set is roughly a third of that.
7 oversized objects were bisected (>50 m radius AND >250k tris), which
caps the largest chunk at 187,655 tris. That is what makes limitChunks a
real lever: the adaptive repo's v5-inst twin, splitting at 800 m instead,
tops out at 782,512 tris in one chunk and the LRU can barely move.
_bands: WHY far IS 900 AND NOT 300, i.e. why geometry looked missing.
The 50/150/300 bands came from the original 2.1 x 1.9 km portla-c5. This
is a 15 x 10 km district cut into OBJECT chunks, whose sizes vary
enormously: radius p10 3.6 m, p50 19 m, p90 112 m, p99 692 m. A chunk
loads by the distance to its SURFACE, so a big object is credited with
its own size and outlives a small object standing on it — by a mean of
1355 m over the 4055 co-located pairs in this manifest. That is the whole
bug: the canopy renders and its poles do not, the stack renders and its
containers do not. Nothing is missing from the bake.
MEASURED, 150 ground cameras, 360° (worst case). A HOLE is an object
whose own chunk is absent while a building-scale chunk covering the same
spot is present:
near/mid/far   resident   encoded   chunk tris   HOLES
Holes fall 98%, and 11.3 MB still sits well under residentBudgetMB.
mid 250 (was 150) costs +0.3 MB and keeps the 150-250 m ring off the far
tier, which is simplifyRatio 0.15 — raising far without raising mid would
have put most of the visible world at the coarsest LOD.
The other half of the fix is in the runtime, not here: ChunkManager
measures surface distance to the bounding BOX rather than the bounding
SPHERE (the sphere is the half-diagonal, so it wildly over-credits
anything elongated). Worth ~a quarter of the total; the BANDS are what
actually closed the gap.

cache._note: REAL DECODED megabytes of GPU-resident geometry + textures, clamped further by the per-device ceiling in streaming/memory.ts (whichever is lower wins). It was 34, but that counted the manifest ENCODED sizes: at the 13.5x decode ratio measured on this bake it meant ~460 MB and the loop never fired. limitChunks is now only a secondary cap on the CPU cache, which is bounded by bytes (memory.ts > cpuMB) — a count cannot bound a set whose chunk radii span 3.6 m to 692 m, and 500 was reasoned against 816 chunks when the cache is keyed by url, of which there are 816 x 3 tiers = 2,448.

_note: THE SECOND STRATEGY over the same manifest — for the layout cameras.
Every layout here is a framing shot with `walkable: false`, authored
54-412 m up and as much as 2.8 km from the terminal. The bands above
are tuned for a person STANDING in it, so from those cameras almost
nothing resolved. Measured, box metric, per layout, chunks inside the
990 m unload radius out of 831:
L01/L02/L03/L07 got 2 chunks each — the water plane and the terrain
plane, the only two whose boxes contain the camera. Everything built
was 1.5-2.8 km away, i.e. outside the radius, so the shot framed sky.
WHY THIS IS CHEAP. The whole model at the far tier is 831 chunks /
22.0 MB encoded / 11.02 M tris, and all 70 images at the 128 px rung
total 0.1 MB. So a radius spanning the entire 15 x 10 km district costs
about 22 MB resident — under the ground config's own 33 MB ceiling.
Measured chunks resolved at far 6000: 831 of 831 from every one of the
ten cameras. Nothing about this needed a second asset set.
far 6000 rather than 4000: 4000 already reaches all ten (826-831), but
6000 spans the district corner-to-corner for the same 22.0 MB, so the
radius stops being a number anyone has to re-check when a camera moves.
near/mid are raised because at this altitude nothing is within 150 m of
the camera anyway — leaving them at 50/250 would have put the whole
frame on the far tier. 150/800 keeps what the shot is composed around
on the mid tier and only the district backdrop on far.
limitChunks 900 (> the 831 total) because all 831 are mounted at once
here: the LRU never evicts a mounted chunk, so a lower ceiling would
simply sit unenforced. The ground config's 500 takes back over on the
way down and evicts to it then.
Only the keys that DIFFER are listed. `streaming` and everything else
not named is inherited from the block above, so a retune there carries
here on its own.
THE OVERVIEW — one fixed camera, the whole model, the coarsest tier.
The dollhouse used to draw `assets.modelUrl`, a separate 11 MB decimated
GLB of the same zone. It now streams the SAME manifest the walking view
does, with `forceTier: far` pinning every chunk to the lowest geometry
LOD and the 128 px rung. Measured on this bake, minus the two hidden
planes: 814 chunks / 22.1 MB encoded / 10.92 M tris for the whole
district — and they are the same bytes first person wants first, so
entering it re-mounts from the decoded-chunk cache rather than parsing a
second model. One asset set now feeds both views.
WHY A PIN AND NOT near/mid AT 0. Both flatten the tiers, but the zeros
also floor the resident-budget loop at `near x 1.5` = 0: a device short
of VRAM would shrink the unload radius to nothing and empty the overview
instead of thinning it. The distances here are the aerial ones, so under
pressure the view degrades from the outside in, from a 225 m floor.
THE BYTES ARE REAL. 22.1 MB encoded decodes to 308 MB of geometry, held
twice (JS heap + GPU) — see streaming/memory.ts. It fits a desktop that
reports >= 8 GB (gpuMB 448); a mid desktop (288) drops the furthest ~7%,
and a phone (96-160) holds a third of it. There is no coarser tier to
fall back to: `far` IS the bottom of this asset set. If the overview has
to be complete on weak hardware, that wants a purpose-baked low-poly
mesh in `assets.modelUrl` and this block deleted.
frustumCull is OFF and alwaysLoadRadiusMetres is 0: the shot is composed
around everything in frame, the orbit turns the camera through 360, and
a cull here would only trade the budget's furthest-first eviction for a
behind-you one. hysteresisMetres is 0 — with one tier there are no band
crossings left to damp.
fog is off. The fade exists so a small download radius does not read as a
wall; here the radius spans the district and there is nothing beyond it
to hide.
HIDE — the two backdrop planes, `water` and `Land_Mesh` in the source
scene. They are 15 x 10 km and 14.5 x 8.6 km against a terminal 1.6 x
1.5 km, so from up here they ARE the frame, and the orbit pivot (the
bbox centre of what is drawn) sits out at sea rather than on the
terminal. They are named by MATERIAL because the bake keeps no mesh
names — see StreamHideRule. On this manifest the rules resolve to c1
(M_Ocean_Water.001, the only chunk carrying it) and c343 (radius
8,427 m); the terminal's own pavement shares c343's material name at
radius 969 m, which is what the minRadiusMetres guard spares.

dollhouse._note: FRAMED BY HAND in the running app and pasted from the pose log — drag the overview with ?debug=true and DollhouseCamera prints this exact line, the `settled` one being the pose you stopped at (rotation as the YXZ euler seatAtHome applies, NOT the XYZ order a GLB tool prints). It started from cp_dolllhouse in la-port-zone-c5-cp-dollhouse.glb and was worked from there. 1,411 m from the zone centre and aimed straight at it, which is what the orbit keeps doing anyway: once the model's world bounds are published the camera re-aims at that centre every frame, so the rotation here only holds until then while the position sets the orbit's radius and angle for good. At `world.fov` 15 that range frames about 370 m of the terminal vertically; the authoring camera carried a 32 degree yfov, so widening the site fov rather than pulling further back is the other way to open the shot.

spawn._note: WHERE FIRST PERSON BEGINS, and where the Home button returns to. Authored rather than derived from startLayoutId because every layout here is an aerial framing (walkable: false — schema-wise, not a valid first-person entry point), so there is no walkable checkpoint to derive it from. It is also the point the streamer fills in around while the entry blackout is up, so moving it changes what you land looking at AND what has finished loading when the fade lifts. TAKEN FROM cp_012 in la-port-zone-c5-cp-v3.glb, via /extract-pos. That file ships twelve cameras; cp_001..cp_010 are the layout framings and cp_012 is this one. The tool prints an XYZ euler and this block stores the YXZ one the runtime applies, so the rotation here is the reorder of [3.0925, -0.0976, 3.1368], not those numbers — re-derive it rather than pasting from the tool. NOT ON THE NAVMESH: its XZ is inside the navmesh-v2 AABB but misses every one of the 3,950 triangles, the nearest vertex being 95.3 m away at [-1227.3, 0.16, -149.4] — which is where the previous spawn sat. Home probes the floor at this XZ and teleports there regardless, so walking OUT of it depends on the snap finding an island. cp_011 in the same file IS on the mesh (surface Y 0.160) if this needs to become walkable.

sky._note: The procedural sky dome (see terminal/scene/environment/sky). `mode` picks a stop on the day arc — "afternoon" is the default, "dusk" the open-sea study's sunset palette, "day" a flat midday one, "off" restores the plain blue backdrop. `t` overrides the stop with an explicit 0..1, and ?debug=true drives it live from a slider. COLOURS ARE NOT AUTHORED HERE: sun direction, sun tint, ambient tint and the sky-fill pair are all derived from the same palette the sky is drawn from, so they cannot drift from it. `lights` is merged over the `lights` block above and is for INTENSITIES — how strongly the model is lit at this hour, which the study (a shader with no scene lights) has no opinion on. `hemiIntensity` is the sky fill that keeps the away-from-sun side off black; raising `ambientIntensity` instead would flatten the lit side.

map._note: TWO RECTS: zone inside site. The map opens framed on `zone` — the walkable area, the only place a click resolves to a route — lifted out of a dimmed surround. Bounds on an image layer name the world coords of its EDGES: minX/maxX are its left/right (X grows rightward, east), minZ/maxZ its top/bottom (Z grows UPWARD, north) — so X reads plainly and only Z is inverted. `site` is the full-port aerial, always dimmed. `plan` is a top-down model render laid over it and is optional: drop the block and the zone still lifts out of the surround, just at the aerial's resolution. PLAN BOUNDS ARE NOT CALIBRATED — they are the exact world AABB of la-port-zone-c5-model-v4_dollhouse-optimized-optimized.glb, which /admin/bounds framed the render to, so world→pixel is exact by construction. A top-down camera with up=+Z puts +X on the LEFT, so the raw render is mirrored east-west; the tool now un-mirrors on export, and this file was flipped by hand because it predates that fix. Cross-checked: the flipped plan's quay, crane rails and rail fans land on the aerial's own, and 93% of the 831 streamed chunk centres fall on plan geometry against a 24% chance level. `zone` is a PLAIN world rect (minX < maxX) because people author it; it is exactly the navmesh AABB.

items.text: Rotate Around to look at the model from different angles
Double Click on the Model to go to First Person View
RESOURCES on the left edge lists every zone and its hotspots
Home returns you to the start point
Dollhouse zooms back out to the overview
Map opens the terminal map — travel anywhere from it
